searchText: Has there been a discussion of increasing the emissions rate for staking yields (above 5%) to incent more staking? We’re still sitting at ~7% staked and seems like that percentage has not really moved up meaningfully in recent weeks I understand the appeal of having ether be deflationary, but does it make sense to increase rewards to stakers to get us closer to a state where the merge is actionable? Right now we’re barely over halfway there I may have missed it in the eth research web portal so if I have, that’s totally my bad I feel like monkeying around with rates would be a bad precedent to set Fair point But in any case, I think when we were coming up with those numbers, the safe min at least I had in mind was 1-5m ETH staking So we're fine Also, withdrawals being available will encourage more staking Also also, validators getting MEV revenue and priority fees will increase de-facto interest rates Ah. So where did the low-teens percentage staked figure come from? Yes exactly The opportunity cost of locking ether right now is very high is there any article teaching how to move ETH to beacon chain and stake it? I don't think we're *insecure* with only a few million ETH staked Maybe the biggest risk is that at a few million, it's easy for a large percentage of that to become a single institution I had made a search some time ago and it seems the only way to stake is being a validator, so one needs to have 32 ETH and build a rid to be able to stake But to the extent you view it as a risk-free asset (or as close to that as you can get in cryptoeconomic land) then 5% is quite reasonable. Lack of liquidity (outside of lido for example) is I think what concerns some people who understand that distinction Or pool. Such as RocketPool, StakeWise Also this: https://lido.fi/ let me take a look Latter i prefer personally due to their tokenomics, but really don't want to be here to advertise services. https://stakewise.medium.com/ https://beaconcha.in/stakingServices You can find other staking services here. Please do your own research. 😄 for sure 😄 https://lido.fi/ethereum is saying they reinvest staked ETH on PoW blockchain DeFi, isn't it meant to move ETH to PoS and be used to validate blocks? well I'll keep waiting for pools more user-friendly service There's really only Rocket Pool as Stakewise in its current form isn't decentralized. Seen their latest announcement? This is exactly what vitalik is warning about. Don't use centralized services. Depends on what your interpretation of decentralised is. DAO with a committee, opening up their nodes to others. Sounds like a good step in the right direction, still giving me the greatest yields and flexibility in opportunities with LP's. That they'll have multiple federated node operators like Lido? If it's easy to collude then it's centralized. Only having a handful of node operators is not much better than only 1. Rocket Pool is very friendly and the only decentralized option, but I don't believe this is the proper channel to be discussing all this. https://stakewise.medium.com/a-new-era-for-stakewise-decentralizing-the-architecture-e598fde75ea8 ^ I'm referring to their newest announcement. agreed, not the channel 😄 That's exactly what I said, a handful of federated nodes. Amazing how we've come to this point where we've been tricked into thinking a handful of nodes is decentralized. This is no different than dPoS, but with less operators. The specific properties to be addressed here are non-custodial management of funds (this can be done with contract based deposit pools and 0x01 withdrawal creds that also point to a contract), and permissionless node operation. Getting blessed to operate a node by a dao does not meet that threshold. A protocol that just requires over-collateralization to run a node goes a long way here to prevent concentration of the network. So I have a general question about where I should make a proposal but I need to give some background: During amphora it was discussed that we would likely use the merge as an opportunity to break the policy that all event logs are stored permanently by full nodes. Pruning logs implies the deposit contract logs will be pruned as well. This is okay because once a deposit becomes finalized in the beacon chain, it will never need to be Merkle proofed on-chain again and it can be discarded. The deposit Merkle tree can be significantly compressed by discarding old deposits and transmitted to newly syncing nodes during weak subjectivity sync. I've implemented this in lighthouse and Zahari has implemented it for Nimbus. Now we want to write something up to explain how to implement this, and get the ball rolling on standardizing the data structure used to transmit the deposit tree, and standardize the beacon API endpoint to fetch the deposit tree. My question is where do I write this? Does this need an EIP?
